newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Motta favors 3-5 Telebras units.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Motta favors 3-5 Telebras units.

text.p: The best way to privatize Brazilian telecommunications holding Telebras would be to split the company into between three and five regional units, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said.

"The creation of a small number of regional-level companies -- that is to say, three to five -- would increase the likelihood of best results from the reform," Motta said in a note accompanying a bill creating a new telecommunications law.

The companies, which would be offered to the private sector as concessions, would be large enough to compete with other Latin American carriers and would stimulate simultaneous investment in telecommunications across Brazil, Motta wrote.
Also, the greater the number of companies, the harder it becomes for one to monopolize the sector, he said.
"It is therefore obvious that scenarios which envision the regionalization of existing state-level firms are preferable to those which see only national-level operators," he said.

Embratel, Telebras' long-distance and international carrier, would continue to operate on a national level. New operators would be allowed into that segment once privatization had progressed, Motta said.

The regional companies would have to be sufficiently large to be of interest to foreign investors who have opportunities in telecommunications privatizations in about 15 other emerging market countries over the next three years, he said.
